summary.title: A Review Process
summary.one_liner: Learn how BuzzFeed's Tech org runs performance reviews: Leadership Principles as a rubric, non-anonymous peer feedback routed through managers, and spreadsheet-based level calibration.
takeaways: Anchor review questions to a small set of company values (Leadership Principles) so reviewers have a rubric instead of a blank page.
Switching from anonymous to non-anonymous peer reviews, routed first through the recipient's manager as an editing layer, can make feedback more specific and conversations more useful.
Calibration sheets, where the employee and manager each rate skill levels and discrepancies are highlighted, make disagreements about level visible and guide goal setting.
Calibration conversations can also reveal gaps in role documentation, which the author uses to iterate on those docs each year.
Start from explicit review goals (self-reflection, collaboration, manager-team alignment, candid culture) and check assumptions with people involved.
summary.summary: Cap Watkins, a design leader at BuzzFeed Tech, describes the review system he has built and administered over about three years, covering both Product Design and the wider Tech org. He starts with the goals the process should meet, then explains how reviews are structured around two questions tied to Leadership Principles adapted from Amazon. He covers the switch to non-anonymous peer reviews that managers compile and share, and the answers he gives to common concerns about harsh or watered-down feedback. He closes with the Product Design "Calibration" spreadsheet process and reflections on iterating the process over time.
